about.title: Laguna Niguel Medical Malpractice Claims
about.longDescription: Medical malpractice cases in Laguna Niguel arise the same way they do anywhere in Orange County — a delayed diagnosis, a surgical slip, a medication mix-up, or a failure to warn about known risks. What makes these claims different from a car crash case is timing and proof: California's MICRA law generally gives patients one year from when they discover the harm, and no more than three years from the injury itself, plus a required 90-day notice before filing suit. Because a qualified medical expert almost always has to weigh in on whether the care fell below an accepted standard, these claims typically move slower and require more documentation than a typical injury case. A bad medical outcome by itself isn't proof of malpractice — the question is whether the provider deviated from what a reasonably careful practitioner would have done. If you're trying to figure out whether what happened to you or a family member in Laguna Niguel might qualify, LawProactive can connect you free with an independent attorney who can review the records and explain your options.

whyChoose.title: Why Understanding MICRA Matters Before You Wait

items.title: Discovery Clock Is Shorter Than You'd Think
items.desc: Because the deadline is generally one year from when you discover the harm, and never more than three years from the injury, waiting to sort out what happened can cost you the ability to file at all.

items.title: 90-Day Notice Requirement
items.desc: California requires a formal 90-day notice to the provider before a malpractice lawsuit can be filed, which means the process has to start well before any court deadline arrives.

items.title: Expert Review Is Almost Always Needed
items.desc: Because a qualified medical expert typically has to confirm the care fell below an accepted standard, an early records review by an attorney's medical resources can clarify whether a claim is worth pursuing.

items.question: I had a bad outcome after surgery near Crown Valley Parkway — does that mean malpractice happened?
items.answer: Not necessarily. A poor result alone isn't evidence of malpractice under California law; the question is whether the provider's care fell below what a reasonably careful practitioner would have done in the same situation. An attorney working with a medical expert can help determine whether your case meets that standard.

items.question: How long do I have to bring a medical malpractice claim in Laguna Niguel?
items.answer: Under MICRA, it's generally one year from when you discover the injury, and no more than three years from when the injury occurred. There's also a required 90-day pre-suit notice to the healthcare provider, so the clock effectively starts running sooner than people expect.

items.question: Is there a cap on what I can recover in a California malpractice case?
items.answer: California law caps non-economic damages, like pain and suffering, though that cap rises each year under current law. Economic damages, such as medical bills and lost income, are generally not subject to that same cap. An attorney can walk you through how this applies to your specific situation.
